topic: Under strict removal ordering the worst
canonical_claim: Under strict removal ordering, the worst cases "two cleanup rows for one namespace" and "a cleanup row with no catalog entry" become unconstructible (both require rebirth before the first removal retired); the worst-case capacity test should be replaced by an anomaly check that fires if GC ever observes an entry-less cleanup row.

topic: The ack floor GC redesign drops
canonical_claim: The ack-floor GC redesign drops `process_epoch` as a separate merged-heartbeat field because the writable path already sets `process_epoch = writer_epoch` (`CasStore.cpp:157`) and the sweep consumes `writer_epoch` unchanged, so a distinct field would be redundant.

topic: The ack floor design renamed the
canonical_claim: The ack-floor design renamed the sabotage control `SabotageDeleteAtFloor` to `SabotageIgnoreAckFloor` because an `r < min_ack` vs `r ≤ min_ack` off-by-one is provably still safe under the publish-order invariant, so the load-bearing control is "ignores the floor entirely", not the exact boundary.

topic: An optional pre pass refresh for
canonical_claim: An optional pre-pass refresh for the promote copy-forward tokenless-blob race fix (spec §3) was deliberately deferred rather than implemented: it is a fast-path-only optimization, not required for correctness, so it was left unscheduled rather than turned into a task.

topic: Before the redesign 100 000 tables
canonical_claim: Before the redesign, 100,000 tables with 8 root shards each required approximately 800,000 CAS-PUTs and 1,600,000 GETs per GC round because the fence and recheck traversed the entire root-shard universe.

topic: Before T2 a snapshot run was
canonical_claim: Before T2, a snapshot run was materialized three times—by `CasObjectStorageBackend::get`, `RunFileReader::full`, and `readPriorEdges`—for peak memory of approximately 3 × O(active edges) per GC shard; the target example estimated about 24 GB RAM for one fold.

topic: Before T0 every pass rewrote every
canonical_claim: Before T0, every pass rewrote every GC-shard snapshot run even for an empty delta, causing an idle pool to pay two snapshot sizes per round; at the target scale and 5-minute rounds this was estimated as terabytes per day of churn.

topic: streaming run reads
canonical_claim: Opening a snapshot run in streaming mode uses a HEAD, a ranged tail GET for the footer, and a body `getStream`; resident run memory is O(block) while the wire bytes are unchanged. Streaming GC run reads use true ranged reads and `getStream`; opening a run costs three requests (`head`, tail `get`, and body `getStream`), or four when a large footer is present, and each `seek` costs one ranged GET per block.

topic: With T0 an idle round that
canonical_claim: With T0, an idle round that has no changes touches zero snapshot-run objects and consists of the LIST sweep, heartbeats, and one `gc/state` CAS.

topic: Idle GC over a static 20M
canonical_claim: Idle GC over a static 20M-row, 400-part pool used about 1,362 `CasGcGet`, 643 `CasBlobHead`, and 457 `CasRootGet` operations per round, roughly 2,500 S3 operations per round despite no changes.

topic: The observed GC round duration grew
canonical_claim: The observed GC round duration grew from 87 ms at 400 parts to 92.6 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at 100,000 parts, demonstrating O(ref-universe/object-count) scaling; fsck also becomes O(objects) and timed out at 100,000 parts.; GC folds remain O(ref-universe) for large deltas: measured duration grew from about 87 ms at 400 parts to 93 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at about 100,000 parts, even though correctness held with `dangling=0`.

topic: Partitioned inserts in S11 require O
canonical_claim: Partitioned inserts in S11 require O(partitions) CAS commits, taking about 10 seconds for a 256-partition insert; deferred GC during 64 delete rounds allowed orphaned parts to outpace disk capacity.

topic: Gc fold performs a streaming two
canonical_claim: `Gc::fold` performs a streaming two-cursor merge over the entire prior generation's source-edge run, reading the whole prior generation and writing a whole new consolidated run even when one edge or no edge changed.

topic: The codecs v3 phase 3 soak
canonical_claim: The codecs-v3 phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, equal oracle counts on both replicas, recovered from four faults and two restarts, and drained the pool from about 3 GB to 102 MB.

topic: The ref intake loop is serial
canonical_claim: The ref-intake loop is serial: approximately 1.9 million requests at 0.9 ms each imply about 1710 seconds, close to the observed 1830-second maximum and consistent with nearly all phase time being serial request latency.

topic: If the approximately 1710 second serial
canonical_claim: If the approximately 1710-second serial fetch floor were parallelized N-way, the ideal fetch component would be about 213.75 seconds at N=8 and 106.875 seconds at N=16, before merge cost.

topic: The ref chain design adds about
canonical_claim: The ref-chain design adds about two serial S3 round trips per committed chunk for `_ckpt`, one conditional PUT per touched namespace per epoch transition during recovery, and one catalog GET per fold round after the hot LIST.

topic: The dominant T15 GC cost was
canonical_claim: The dominant T15 GC cost was `defer_decision`: 5,096.39 seconds, 79.11% of GC time, including full LISTs of about 177,000 keys even when `changed_shards` was zero.

topic: Across 65 263 ref log uploads
canonical_claim: Across 65,263 ref-log uploads in the affected namespace, partitioned by epoch, zero uploads were out of order.

topic: The GC cadence tradeoff is approximately
canonical_claim: The GC cadence tradeoff is approximately `A/interval + B·interval`, where `A` is per-fold universe work and `B` is writer amplification from journal growth; the proposed optimal interval scales as `sqrt(U) / r` for blob universe `U` and hottest-shard mutation rate `r`.

topic: The system cas_gc_log counters entries_condemned entries_graduated
canonical_claim: The `system.cas_gc_log` counters `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, and `entries_redeleted` represent the three retired-cursor pipeline stages: newly condemned, floor-passed and republished `delete_pending`, and executed exact-token blob deletes.

topic: The outstanding reconciliation debt recorded 56
canonical_claim: The outstanding reconciliation debt recorded 56 already-leaked blobs that incremental rounds could never reclaim because their in-degree was pinned above zero; only rebuilding in-degree state could reclaim them.

topic: Before generation retention B174 was added
canonical_claim: Before generation retention (B174) was added, a 12h soak measured `gc/` bookkeeping at 82% of pool storage (2822 retained generations, roughly 3.7 MiB/shard/generation), dwarfing actual data 8:1.

topic: GC observability gained per phase timing
canonical_claim: GC observability gained per-phase timing during Stage B, which immediately found the fold seal being read five times per round where the design intended two.

topic: The measured GET cost formula for
canonical_claim: The measured GET-cost formula for a folding GC round is exact: total `S3GetObject` = ref-log body GETs + manifest body GETs, i.e. `1 + edges_per_log`, which climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows; round trips equal `logs + edges` at a flat roughly 0.5 ms per round trip across a 140x request range, and a measured 416-round `Success` sample cost roughly $0.007 in total S3 charges.
